text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

The panel composition points nowhere useful: you and the successful candidate are both women, so your sex can't explain why she was chosen over you. An all-women panel favouring a woman over another woman is statistically unremarkable and raises no inference. Raising it would likely read as grievance-hunting and damage your standing for future competitions.

The real anomaly is the unanswered request. Two weeks' silence on a written explanation of a competitive public-sector appointment is worth pursuing — resend in writing, cc the HR director or clerk, cite any local policy or access-to-information right, and ask specifically how the posted qualifications were weighted. "Extensive public consultation experience" may indicate the panel prioritised something your file undersold. That's the question to ask.
